title: Spain Isn’t The Only One Taking Home Gold This Week — Louis Vuitton Just Dropped The Ultimate Trophy Trunk
text:
Spain Isn’t The Only One Taking Home Gold This Week — Louis Vuitton Just Dropped The Ultimate Trophy Trunk

If last night’s electric football thriller proved anything, it’s that sports culture and high fashion are officially fused, and Spain isn’t the only one taking home gold this week.

Fresh off the post-match adrenaline, Louis Vuitton just unveiled its official bespoke Trophy Trunk and exclusive capsule collection for the FIFA World Cup 2026. Because if you’re carrying the world’s most coveted sporting prize across the Atlantic Ocean, a standard carry-on simply won’t cut it.

Handcrafted in the historic Asnières-sur-Seine workshops, the custom trunk is wrapped in LV’s signature Monogram canvas, featuring hand-painted gold panels that form a hard-to-miss “V” for both Victory and Vuitton, of course. Brass corner protectors and a plush beige leather lining dial up the luxury factor.

For those of us not personally lifting the FIFA trophy, the Maison is bringing the high-stakes aesthetic into our own homes. Louis Vuitton’s limited-edition lineup includes the Coffret 8 Montres, Cotteville 16 Montres, and iconic Malle Courrier Lozine 110. And for the ultimate personal touch, each can be customized with your own initials.

As game-day fashion evolves from a street-style trend into full-fledged luxury couture, this collaboration marks the ultimate intersection of elite athletic triumph and timeless French craftsmanship. Whether you’re a die-hard supporter celebrating Spain’s reign or just looking to elevate your travel style, one thing is clear: luxury sports aesthetic has officially entered its golden era.

title: The Japanese Manicure Is The Natural Way To Stronger, Healthier Nails
text:
The Japanese Manicure Is The Natural Way To Stronger, Healthier Nails

There’s always something keeping us entertained in the nail world. So far this year, we’ve spotted innovations like Hard BIAB, a type of reinforced builder gel that adds serious strength and structure to your nails, not to mention an abundance of nail trends, like the “phantom” French manicure and chrome croc nails. Most of these techniques are all geared towards nail aesthetics, lending themselves to cool custom designs or colors. Rarely are they a targeted remedy for dry, brittle and weak nails. Until recently, that is. Say hello to the Japanese manicure.

What is the Japanese manicure? 

We first reported on the Japanese manicure in 2024, but it has a long history. It’s a ritualistic experience first and foremost, says nail expert Gabriella Ferenczi from Figaro London. Often referred to as ‘P.Shine’ after the company that brought the ritual to the masses, the method is thought to date back around 400 years in Japan.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Sweet Treat Vienna (@sweettreatvienna)

The Japanese manicure has one main aim: to improve the health of your nails and give them a beautiful pearlescent finish, like these nails posted to Instagram by @sweettreatvienna. “In essence, it’s about massaging nutrients deep into your nail plate to make your nails super healthy so that they shine on their own without the need for a drop of polish,” explains Ferenczi. The method doesn’t promise any additional nail length or out-there nail art. Instead, it can transform neglected, weak nails, especially those that have been subjected to gels or acrylics.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by NAILS BROWS AMSTERDAM (@ma.mi.nails)

We’re talking strictly kind-to-the-nail tools, no harsh solvents and absolutely zero nail polish. You might be thinking, so what’s the point? It’s all in the name of nail health. Given that many of us go against every nail technician’s wish of using cuticle oil every day, it’s just the ticket for breathing life into dry, damaged nail beds and turning them into pearly new canvases. Take inspiration from these nails posted to Instagram by @ma.mi.nails.

@nails.and.brows Japanese manicure to strengthen your nails and give it extra shine ✨💫 #kuwait🇰🇼 #japanesemanicure #nailsandbrow #nailskuwait #fypシ゚ #الكويت ♬ we cant be friends – 🫧

In line with the manicure’s age-old roots, no metal tools or solvents are used throughout the process. “Only ceramic nail files and traditional polishing units and natural oils are used,” says Ferenczi. As this is a very old practice, some salons enlist deer or calfskin files and cloths. However, nowadays, many salons opt for cruelty-free tools, and if you’re doing this at home, you can just use a simple nail buffer. 

London-based session manicurist Ami Streets says: “It really brings the manicure routine back to basics. You’re incorporating the application of oils, pushing back (but not cutting) the cuticles and providing a hand massage.” Not only does the Japanese manicure impart a beautifully groomed aesthetic, but it also gives nails a break from the use of electric tools (potentially damaging if used incorrectly) or nail polish formulas (which can often stain), adds Streets. “It’s great for rest periods between gel polish or extensions, as you can get nails and hands back into optimum condition.”

What happens during the Japanese manicure? 

The first step in a traditional Japanese manicure is cleansing and shaping your nails with a nail file, and pushing the cuticles back. A gentle cuticle remover may also be used here, whether a lotion or a snipping tool.

Next, the nail plate is smoothed using a buffer and a stiff brush. Thirdly, a green paste is applied onto the nail plate. It’s typically made from a mix of vitamins A and E, bee pollen, keratin (a protein found naturally in nails) and silica (a mineral from the Sea of Japan), explains Ferenczi. “It has a characteristic green color and also contains different oils such as jojoba, bamboo, ylang-ylang and red tea.” This is then gently buffed in using a chamois (a natural leather) tool. 

@alextt_99 #japanesemanicure #pshine #nailsnailsnails #naturalnails ♬ original sound – Alex

Once all the nails have been buffed with the paste, the manicurist gently buffs a mineral powder into each nail plate, again with the chamois. The powder (often known as P.Shine powder) is made from diatomaceous earth (a naturally occurring, soft sedimentary rock that can be crumbled into a fine powder) as well as beeswax, explains Ferenczi. “It’s used to seal in the nutrients from the paste and to give the nails a slight pink sheen that lasts for about two weeks.”

When combined, the paste and powder trap in moisture and nutrients to lend the most incredible gleam. It’s hard to believe the result isn’t actually caused by a high-shine top coat. The final step is a good hand massage using thick creams and cuticle oils. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Line Spa and Polish (@linespaandpolish)

Can the Japanese manicure help weak nails?  

That’s exactly what it can do. “The Japanese manicure is essentially a strengthening treatment for brittleness,” says Ferenczi. The ingredients in both the powder and paste are great for reinforcing weak nails. “Beeswax in particular is an excellent emollient, which means it retains moisture,” says Streets, while the addition of keratin can help to rebuild the nail structure. 

The hand massage is also important. “Using nourishing products will result in smooth, hydrated and healthy skin, as well as strong, flexible nails that withstand wear and tear and can grow,” says Streets. When it comes to moisturizing your hands, Streets adds, consistency is key.

@lemaribeauty Japanese manicure, from dull nails to shiny, without using nail varnish 👌🏼#españa #españa #tenerife #manicura #beauty ♬ Do It To It – ACRAZE

Streets predicts that treatments like the Japanese manicure are only going to grow in popularity, and Ferenczi agrees. “We definitely see a demand for health-conscious manicures where the focus is on natural ingredients,” she says. “The Japanese manicure is a good choice for someone who wants to take a break from extensions and gel polish, especially.”

How much is the Japanese manicure and how long does it last?

The best thing about the Japanese manicure is that it’s speedy. Usually the method only takes around 30 minutes. To find a salon that offers the Japanese manicure near you, head to the salon app, Booksy. Prices will vary from salon to salon, but as the treatment is short and doesn’t include any polish application, you can expect it to cost less than your usual manicure. Similar to gel polish, the naturally glossy effect of the Japanese manicure lasts up to two weeks.

If you fancy giving this manicure a go at home, you can buy the P.Shine kit from Amazon, but it might set you back a little more than a regular buffer, which you can get from somewhere like Ulta. Try the Revlon Shape ‘N’ Buff File & Buffer, which has file, buff, and shine edges. When it comes to sealing in moisture, R29 rates Sally Hansen Cuticle Massage Cream, with beeswax, similar to the paste used in a professional Japanese manicure. Lastly, a great hand cream is a must. Try L’Occitane Nourishing and Protective Shea Butter Hand Cream with moisturizing glycerin, shea butter, and a handful of oils.

title: Leo Season Is Here — & Get Ready For A Spiritual Awakening Of A Lifetime
text:
Leo Season Is Here — & Get Ready For A Spiritual Awakening Of A Lifetime

The height of the summer season is upon us, bringing the heat and theatrics, too. The sun shakes up our lives as it enters the zodiac sign of Leo on July 22nd. For the next four weeks, we will roar louder than we have in the past because the celestial forces above are stirring up chaos for us earthlings (very fitting for Leo’s solar return, right?). Get ready for the spiritual awakening of a lifetime because the planets are coming in hot to ensure we release fear and step into a new emotional space.

The sun in Leo connects with three planets on July 27th: Uranus in Gemini, Neptune retrograde in Aries, and Pluto retrograde in Aquarius. Power struggles and jealousies will persist, pushing us to confront matters that have been swept under the rug and for far too long. The issue is that our desire to escape reality and to not deal with these types of situations creates tension with others. But the emotional bubble will burst, ending with a confrontation. The other way to look at this aspect is to be honest and open by engaging in the hard conversations that need to be had. 

On July 29th, the day of the Full Buck Moon, Jupiter forms a “cazimi” [a Latin term that translates to “the heart of the sun”] union with the sun, magnifying the influence of the expansive planet. Jupiter is known as the “greater benefic”; however, its effects can be both positive and negative. The favorable element of Jupiter brings fortune, abundance, and luck, but the adverse traits enhance circumstances that might be best left as they are. Watch out for indulgence and excess to avoid destructive habits. The day could go either way — overall, it’s going to be intense with the other aspects coming to light from the lunation. 

The sun in Leo harmonizes with Saturn retrograde in Aries on August 6th. We might feel as though restrictions and obstacles stand in the way of how we want to live. Limits may be placed on our freedoms, making us less confident than usual. This is only a moment in time, so doing affirmative work that boosts our self-esteem is ideal. Be less critical and more kind to yourself. 

August 12th’s total solar eclipse in Leo is a transformational cosmic phenomenon that will rock our word. We are taking stock of how we can move above and beyond the present to cultivate a beautiful future. The journey there could be messy if we refuse to refresh our dreams and goals. We’ll feel the energy of the eclipse until August 22nd, when the sun in Leo opposes the North Node of Destiny in Aquarius, ushering us to a new state of being. 

Important dates during Leo Season:

July 22nd: The sun enters Leo, adding flair and fire to our auras. Take center stage and shine as bright as the sun!

July 23rd: Mercury turns direct in Cancer, tracing over the degrees it visited in the previous month. The retroshade phase, which lasts until August 6th, gives us a chance to clear up miscommunications and mishaps.

July 26th: Saturn retrograde in Aries offers us a moment to redefine boundaries and the periphery of our careers. 

July 26th: The North Node of Destiny moves into Aquarius, and the South Node of Destiny glides into Aquarius, inviting us to innovate our visions and focus on the community. 

July 29th: The Full Buck Moon in Aquarius brings immense growth and development that is vital for us to undergo. 

August 6th: Venus shifts into Libra, evoking our romantic sentiments and yearning to find balance in all we do.

August 9th: Mercury gets passionate in the sign Leo, making big declarations that we may not be able to fulfill — be careful and do not overpromise. 

August 11th: Mars swims into Cancer, softening our reactions and urging us to be protective of our energy.

August 12th: The total solar eclipse in Leo is an opportunity to release and evolve — if we are ready for it.

August 22nd: The sun enters Virgo, grounding our senses and allowing us to be pragmatic in our lives.

title: Your Horoscope This Week: July 19 To 26
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: July 19 To 26

Welcome to one of the most empowering weeks of July, cosmic beings. The week begins with Jupiter, the planet of abundance, forming a beautiful trine to Neptune, the planet of dreams, reminding us that some opportunities are simply too meaningful to keep postponing. If there’s a dream you’ve been nurturing, this is your invitation to take one bold step toward it. That same day, however, Jupiter opposes Pluto, revealing the inner fears, limiting beliefs, and self-sabotaging patterns that may try to convince you you’re not ready. This isn’t a battle between good luck and bad luck. It’s a choice between trusting your potential and continuing to let old stories decide what’s possible. Dream boldly, but stay rooted in reality. Confidence grows strongest when it’s supported by preparation, self-awareness, and intentional action.

On July 21st, the First Quarter Moon in Libra reminds us that progress often requires adjustment rather than perfection. If something feels out of balance, this is your chance to make a thoughtful course correction before pushing ahead. At the same time, Jupiter forms a harmonious aspect with Uranus, bringing unexpected opportunities, exciting conversations, and refreshing breakthroughs that reward flexibility. Stay open to pleasant surprises this week. The opportunity you’re hoping for may arrive in a form you hadn’t considered.

The energy becomes noticeably lighter as the week comes to a close. The sun enters Leo on July 22nd, Mercury stations direct on July 23rd, and Leo Season officially comes alive with Jupiter already blazing through the sign. After weeks of reflection, hesitation, and revision, momentum begins returning. This is your reminder to stop shrinking your gifts, hiding your talents, or waiting for permission to be seen. The final days of this week are filled with courage, creativity, and confidence. Take up space, celebrate your progress, and let yourself be witnessed. The second half of 2026 is asking you to lead with your heart, trust your light, and remember that your authenticity is one of your greatest strengths.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, this week’s First Quarter Moon in Libra reminds you that every meaningful relationship eventually asks for honesty. The moon lands in your partnership sector, bringing the first real checkpoint since last week’s Cancer New Moon. If you’ve been avoiding a conversation, waiting for someone else to make the first move, or struggling to balance your own needs with someone else’s, this lunation encourages you to address it with openness instead of assumption. You don’t have to solve everything overnight, but you do need to be clear about where you stand. The strongest relationships aren’t the ones without friction — they’re the ones where both people are willing to keep choosing each other through it.

Then in the week’s second half, Leo Season begins on July 22nd, activating your romance, fame, and inner child sector, while Mercury stations direct in your home and family zone the very next day. The emotional fog you’ve been navigating begins to lift, making it easier to move forward with confidence. It’s time to share the creative project, flirt a little, laugh more, and let yourself be seen. The more joy you allow yourself to experience now, the more naturally you’ll step into the momentum that’s waiting for you as July comes to a close.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, your daily routine is asking for a tune-up, not a complete renovation. The First Quarter Moon in Libra activates your wellness, habits, and work zone, bringing your attention to the little things that shape your quality of life. If you’ve been trying to do everything perfectly, this is your reminder that consistency beats intensity every time. Maybe it’s going to bed thirty minutes earlier, taking your lunch break instead of working through it, or finally scheduling the appointment you’ve been putting off. Small adjustments made this week have a way of snowballing into big results. Future you is already saying thank you.

By the second half of the week, the energy feels noticeably lighter. Leo Season begins the 22nd, illuminating your home and family sector alongside Jupiter, making this a beautiful time to create a life that feels just as good behind closed doors as it looks from the outside. Some Taureans will feel called to move, redecorate, renovate, or spend more intentional time with family, while others will simply realize that peace has become one of their biggest definitions of success. Then Mercury stations direct in your communication realm, and suddenly conversations start flowing again. Texts stop getting misread, plans come together more easily, and yes— your dry sense of humor finally lands the way you intended instead of making everyone wonder if they should be offended.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, this week’s First Quarter Moon in Libra reminds you that joy deserves to be taken as seriously as your responsibilities. The moon activates your creativity, romance, and inner child zone, bringing the first checkpoint since last week’s Cancer New Moon. If you’ve been waiting for the “perfect” moment to share your work, ask someone out, pick up a forgotten hobby, or simply do something because it makes you happy, this is your sign. The little voice telling you it’s impractical or that you should be doing something more productive doesn’t get to make every decision. Your creativity is trying to show you the way forward, and the more you trust it, the more momentum you’ll build over the next six months.

By the second half of the week, life starts flowing in your favor again. On the 22nd Leo Season begins, lighting up your communication sector alongside Jupiter, making your ideas bigger, your confidence stronger, and your voice much harder to ignore. Then Mercury, your ruling planet, stations direct in your money realm, and you can practically hear your wallet exhale. If the past few weeks felt like money came in only to disappear just as quickly, or you’ve been playing financial Tetris trying to make everything fit, relief is on the way. Fresh ideas, unexpected opportunities, and smarter ways of creating income begin finding you again. You’ve always had a knack for making something out of nothing, and now the cosmos is finally giving you a little more room to work your magic.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, this week’s First Quarter Moon reminds you that the life you’re building begins with the foundation you’re standing on. The moon activates your home, family, and emotional foundation zone, bringing the first checkpoint since last week’s New Moon in your sign. If you’ve been setting intentions around creating a greater sense of peace, this is where you begin putting them into practice. You may need to have an honest conversation with a family member, reorganize your living space, or simply acknowledge that your emotional needs deserve as much attention as everyone else’s. The more supported you feel in your private life, the easier everything else begins to flow.

By the second half of the week, the energy shifts in a refreshing way. Leo Season begins the 22nd, activating your money and self-worth sector alongside Jupiter, opening the door to greater abundance, confidence, and opportunities to grow your income over the coming year. Then Mercury stations direct in your sign the next day, and it feels like you’re finally coming back to yourself. The mental fog begins lifting, conversations become easier, and decisions that felt impossible a few weeks ago suddenly seem much more straightforward. Trust yourself again. You’ve spent the retrograde gathering wisdom, and now you’re ready to move forward with a clearer mind and a stronger sense of what you truly deserve.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, the First Quarter Moon in Libra reminds you that your voice deserves to be heard. This lunation activates your communication zone, bringing the first meaningful checkpoint since last week’s Cancer New Moon. A conversation may need to happen, a message may need to be shared, or you may simply realize you’ve been sitting on an idea that’s ready to leave your notebook and enter the real world. Trust yourself enough to speak with clarity rather than waiting until everything feels perfect. Every meaningful dream begins with someone being willing to say it out loud, and this week, that someone is you.

Then your favorite time of year officially arrives. Leo Season begins on July 22nd, and with Jupiter already in your sign, you’re stepping into one of the most expansive, joyful, and fortunate chapters you’ve experienced in over a decade. title: Honey Pot’s Bea Dixon Treats Business As a Spiritual Practice
text:
Honey Pot’s Bea Dixon Treats Business As a Spiritual Practice

For the founder of The Honey Pot, Beatrice Dixon, her business is quite literally a dream come true. After battling bacterial vaginosis, a common but uncomfortable infection that disrupts the vaginal microbiome, for months, Dixon’s grandmother came to her in a dream with a list of ingredients that would cure her. On this episode of Go Off Sis, we learn how Dixon went from mixing potions in her home to building a wellness empire with products found in some of the biggest stores across the country. 

If it felt slightly jarring to read about vaginal health right off the jump, well, Dixon knows that. Part of her journey to build The Honey Pot into a multimillion-dollar business began with making folks more comfortable sharing how they’re feeling in their bodies; what’s working for them and what’s not, what’s uncomfortable and what’s confounding. “ I was having that conversation just by telling my story,” Dixon says of her early days selling products face-to-face at fairs and festivals. With her signature mix of honesty, faith, and discipline, she worked with her “co-founder brother” Simon Grey to expand the line to include products for periods, post-partum, sex, and more. 

For Dixon, building a business was a balancing act of trusting in herself and not fully knowing what she was getting into, and the limiting beliefs that would have come with it.  She describes it as being ignorant, but with rules for yourself, and above all, confidence. “ I think that it’s really important that there is, like, an undeniable, unshakable, religious, almost crazy, insane belief in yourself, because you have to believe that you can do anything,” she shares. Belief alone isn’t enough, and running a business isn’t for everybody. Dixon has always been a hard worker, but building an empire hasn’t been without its challenges and growing pains. From making everything herself (and working her day job at Whole Foods) to expanding the line, to waking up at all hours of the day to talk to manufacturers overseas, scaling a business has meant sacrificing nights at home, time with loved ones, and, of course, pushing back on the systems that keep Black women out of business. 

But what keeps Dixon going is her conviction in Honey Pot’s products and what they mean to people. That putting a product out into the community creates a soul tie between her and the customer. “ I think the thing that’s most important to remember is that if we’re making products and we’re putting them in stores, we’re serving humanity. That is a very spiritual thing to do,” she shares. “ If we’re gonna be doing things for people, we have to do it properly. Don’t be out here acting like this doesn’t matter. It matters.”
